research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from player talent and role counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
play-type and role labels derived from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Are organizer/shaper/terminal labels derivable from the play-by-play without using the outcomes they are later used to explain?
Does within-team lineup role coverage vary enough, at adequate exposure, to be estimated?
Is role coverage separable from talent and from role counts once team identity and lineup composition are controlled?
Does a talent control behave when it is itself built from the same possession graph used to define roles?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type classifier produced SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP at 100% makes and TRANSITION 0.62 PPP because the assisted flag exists only on makes; after a rewrite SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. Recorded as an engineering discovery that contaminated simulation.

Label audit overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most play types above the PPP benchmark band, and MIA identity checks failing. Foul possessions leak into OTHER. Verdict recorded as tool_eval_fail.

Inferred defensive-scheme labels showed a change in 61.0% of within-game and 67.7% of cross-game units, with near-uniform transition matrices. The record states the label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently.

Series-level AVOID share vs winning: game-level rho=-0.19 (p=0.008) with inflated n and team-quality confounding; series-level rho=-0.26 (p=0.07, n=50), underpowered, with about 80 series stated as needed for p<0.05. Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Persistent-impact gate failed decay sanity: play-type lifts were flat across lags (about +0.015 to +0.021), within-team lag-1 effects were near zero, Cohen d about 0.01-0.03, with p near 0 driven by n>150k. Flat lifts collapsed under within-team baseline, consistent with team-quality confounding. Verdict failed_gate.

Star-initiator lineup and forced-play-type suppression cells (for example Jokic vs MIN PPP 0.814, n=59) were reported with no placebo or matching. Later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Mechanism recorded as unclear.
Three-level counter ranking (population, team, matchup) gave disagreeing best counters across levels; L1 n_mu ranged 5 to 696 and playoff matchups 4 to 44. Recorded as limited by small samples.
Joint vs sequential ranking: joint pick matched sequential 80.3% of the time; mean PPP left on table +0.020 overall (+0.099 on reroutes). Verdict recorded as descriptive, n=2,779 triggers.
Team AVOID share ranged 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC) across 55 series; player samples 10-178 possessions. No outcome test was run. Verdict recorded as descriptive.
Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap of +0.427 (n>=10 per tier) was in the same direction as the team-level gap, but only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers, and most star cells were below the gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Deriving play-type labels from play-by-play fields that depend on the outcome (assisted flag) and then evaluating PPP by those labels
failed_approaches.why: Assisted flag exists only on makes, so labels were mechanically tied to points; recorded as C_artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels as a validated basis for downstream adaptation findings
failed_approaches.why: OTHER share too high, low-confidence share large, foul possessions leaked into OTHER, identity checks failed; recorded as LIM:label_or_classification_error and LIM:leakage.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred defensive labels to detect scheme change
failed_approaches.why: Label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution; near-uniform transitions consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Cross-possession decay test of play-type effects without within-team baseline
failed_approaches.why: Flat lifts and team-quality confounding; recorded as C_artifact, LIM:confounding.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level tendency-vs-winning test with team quality uncontrolled
failed_approaches.why: Talent confound; n=50 underpowered (p=0.07); recorded as A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Lineup-level star suppression claims without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: No placebo; PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE risk; mechanism unclear.

evidence_establishes: Play-type and derived labels built from this play-by-play have repeatedly failed validation (leakage, label error, OTHER inflation), so any role label needs its own audit before use.
Team-quality and talent confounds have repeatedly produced apparent effects that vanished under within-team baselines in this project's earlier work.
Per-player or per-matchup cells with n<30 in both tiers were not sufficient for stable inference in earlier work.
Earlier work on the adjacent question (tendency, counters, play-type lifts) did not test organizer/shaper/terminal coverage.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record defines organizer, shaper, or terminal roles or measures lineup role coverage.
No record estimates within-team variance in role coverage, so whether the first clause holds is unknown.
No record shows that talent control, as it would be built here, is valid or stable.
Whether role coverage is separable from role counts is not addressed by any record.
Retrieved records are truncated in places ('[cut; read_family for the full text]'), so some details may be missing.
own_inferences: The question bundles three separate claims (within-team variation, separability, talent-control behavior); each needs its own test, and failure of one blocks the others.
Role labels built from the same possessions whose points are later modeled would be outcome-derived, so the separability claim could be true by construction.
With 90 team-seasons, the number of within-team contrasts is limited, and most team-seasons would need to be split by lineup to get usable cells, which the earlier n>=30 gates suggest is hard.
A talent measure built from player-level PPP would share the outcome, so talent control could absorb role effects.
uncertainties: The exact definitions of organizer, shaper, and terminal are not in the retrieved material.
Data catalog fields were not retrieved, so it is unknown whether minutes and partial possessions are enough for lineup-level exposure.
Whether the 2025-26 partial data should be included is not settled.
No record reports the within-team variance or the lineup exposure distribution for role coverage.
Retrieved records have no validation recorded (NOT_RECORDED).

historical_effect.explanation: Earlier records of label artifacts (SF-PAP-096, SF-APPM-014), talent confounding (SF-CHT-039, SF-CHT-029), and small-sample failures (SF-APPS-036, SF-APPM-055) showed that a direct test of the question as posed would likely reproduce these failure modes. This moved the decision from proceeding to a test to not proceeding with the question as posed, and toward a label-audit-first design.

blocking_constraints.text: Organizer/shaper/terminal labels would be derived from the same possession graph and points used as outcomes, so separability from outcomes cannot be established.
Earlier play-type labels failed audit (OTHER 20.2%, foul leakage, identity failures); role labels inherit this risk.
Talent and team quality confound lineup effects; earlier within-team baselines collapsed apparent effects.
90 team-seasons and lineup-level cells gated at n>=30 leave few usable within-team contrasts.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record addresses lineup coverage of organizer, shaper, or terminal roles, its within-team variation, its separability from talent and counts, or talent-control behavior. The cited records cover adjacent play-type, counter, and defensive-label questions, and their findings bear on methodological risks (label validity, confounding, power) rather than on the question itself.

risks.text: Role labels built from points-bearing possession records make separability from outcomes circular.
Labels using future possession content (for example, initiator outcomes or assisted flags) can leak the result into the predictor.
Inferred role labels may misclassify possessions, as the play-type audit already showed.
Team quality and player talent move together with lineup role composition; without within-team baselines, apparent coverage effects are expected to collapse.
Lineup-by-role cells are sparse; prior gates (n>=30) left only a few usable cells.
Minutes per lineup and role coverage may be too thin in many team-seasons to estimate within-team variation.
Role coverage and talent measures may not be stable across seasons or between regular season and playoffs.
Star-lineup suppression findings lacked placebo checks, so any positive role-coverage result would need placebo comparison.
Three sub-claims plus multiple role definitions and lineup cuts raise the risk of chance findings.
Seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 and regular vs playoff data may differ in roster and style, and 2025-26 playoffs are partial until 2026-06-21.
The play-type classifier was rewritten after producing artifacts; similar pipeline bugs could affect role labels.

design.estimand: Not defined for the question as posed. The minimum viable step is a label-validity audit: the agreement and stability of organizer/shaper/terminal labels, built from pre-possession information only, against independent benchmarks. Only after that would the separability and talent-control claims be estimable.
design.unit: Possession for the label audit; lineup-by-team-season for coverage; team-season for the within-team contrast.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23 to 2024-25 (complete). Playoffs and 2025-26 excluded until complete (2025-26 regular season from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs from 2026-06-21). Use the 90 team-seasons as recorded.
design.power: Not established. Before any hypothesis test, check that enough lineup-level cells pass a pre-specified minimum-possession gate (for example n>=30 in each role-coverage category) to estimate within-team variation. Report the count and the power for the minimum detectable within-team effect; do not proceed if the usable cell count is too small.
design.controls: Team fixed effects for the within-team contrast; player-level talent measured from a source independent of the possessions used for role labels (for example, prior-season or box-score-only measures); role counts entered explicitly; lineup minutes as exposure; placebo role assignments (shuffled within team and season).
design.falsification: The label audit fails if role labels agree with independent benchmarks at or below chance, or if labels change when the outcome fields are removed. The separability claim fails if role coverage effects vanish after talent and role-count controls, or if placebo assignments produce comparable effects.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the role definitions, the lineup gate, and the single primary contrast; correct for any secondary contrasts (Holm or BH).
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a hypothesis test only if (1) role labels pass the audit without outcome fields, (2) enough within-team cells pass the gate, and (3) placebo assignments show no comparable effect. Otherwise report the question as untestable with this data.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25, with the 2025-26 regular season excluded until complete (from 2026-04-13). Playoffs and 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete. Record the exact file versions and the play-type graph build date.

methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and role counts?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
